Project rules: commit and push each verified change straight to main (no PRs), with the attribution line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`; short plain-English commit messages. Docs must never claim more than the code does, and must never invent people, emails or partners that don't exist.

Task:
Your area: docs only. Audit rows: "Contributor on-ramp", "Licences and model card", and the DPG quick wins in the appendix.

Setup: other sessions share this checkout, so work in your own worktree: `git -C ward fetch && git -C ward worktree add "../ward-wt-docs" -b contributor-docs origin/main` and work only there.

1. `CONTRIBUTING.md` (DCO sign-off, how to run tests, how slang-pack and lesson changes are reviewed), `LANGUAGES.md` (who maintains what; today nobody), and `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` forms for helpline update, slang word, false alarm, translation and bug. Every form warns "never paste a real child's chat". Add a `config.yml` pointing safety concerns to SAFEGUARDING.md.
2. Draft 6 to 10 seed issues as a markdown file (`docs/SEED_ISSUES.md`). **Don't create them on GitHub, and don't change repo settings or labels.**
3. A model card for Ward Lite (`train/MODEL_CARD.md`): data, intended use, out-of-scope use, in-distribution caveat, the red-team weaknesses, and raise-only authority. Use numbers from `README.md`/`docs/REDTEAM.md` as they stand on main. Another session is rerunning them, so link to them rather than copying long tables.
4. A licence column in `train/DATA.md` for every dataset (SentNoB is CC BY-ND; CB1 unknown; mteb undeclared), stating the consequence plainly and what replacing SentNoB would take. A content licence proposal (CC BY 4.0) as a clearly marked owner decision, not applied.
5. DPG.md quick wins: cite SDG 4.a.2, split Gemma 4 (Apache 2.0) from ShieldGemma (Gemma Terms), e5-small is MIT. Link the new docs from README in one short line, and touch nothing else in README (another session is editing its scorecard section).

Fill no contact placeholders with made-up addresses; list them as owner to-dos. Run `pnpm test`, then push to main (fetch, rebase onto origin/main, push; retry on rejection). Finish with a short report: commits, plus the list of owner-only to-dos you found.

Ward

A guardian that lives on a child's own device. It spots cyberbullying in English, Roman Urdu,
Hinglish and Bangla, keeps the evidence, coaches the next step, and trains kids to bounce back.
Open-weight Gemma, running locally. No server and no account: a child's messages never go to us or to any AI company.

No release yet. Until the first version is published, build Ward from source.

The bully is the ghost haunting the chat. Ward is the ghost on your side. Before you put Ward in front of a child, read the draft [safeguarding policy](docs/SAFEGUARDING.md): what Ward will never do, what hasn't been reviewed by a child-protection professional yet, and [how to raise a concern](docs/SAFEGUARDING.md#10-raising-a-concern-about-the-project-itself). ## What this is, and what it isn't Ward is a response to World Solve problem [WS05937](https://www.worldsolve.org/index.php?view=problem&id=5937): *Building effective interventions for cyberbullying harming children by 2030*, built for the DEV Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge, Week 4 (*Ghost in the Machine*). **It doesn't solve cyberbullying.** Nothing built in a week could. What's here is: 1. **An MVP** that works: a child-owned app for Android, desktop and the web, tested on the device and in CI. 2. **An approach** with numbers behind it: a scorecard showing open-weight Gemma reads abuse in the languages these children type, where an English-first safety model goes blind. 3. **A path** to an intervention that helps children at scale, including what's missing and how we'd measure whether children are actually better off: [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md). The evidence is clear that apps alone don't fix bullying. School-wide programs that involve peers and teachers do best, and even they cut cyberbullying modestly (g = -0.13 to -0.18 across 50 studies). So Ward is built as the child's front door into the people who can help: the adult they tell, their class, and helplines. ## Three rings ### The child | | | | --- | --- | | **Share to Ward** | In WhatsApp, *Export chat* and pick Ward from the share list (Android). Or paste messages, or drop screenshots on a computer running Gemma through Ollama. Say which person is you. | | **Reads on the phone** | Ward Lite, a 38 MB model inside the app, reads every message offline. On a computer, Gemma 4 reads with context and can tell banter from bullying. On Android phones with 6 GB+, Gemma 4 E2B can be downloaded to help write. | | **See the pattern** | One mean message is rude; bullying is a pattern. Ward finds the same person again and again, pile-ons, accounts added to a group just to attack ("ghost accounts"), exclusion, attacks after 11pm, and dangerous messages (threats, telling someone to hurt themselves, sexual pressure, threats to share photos). | | **The Haunting** | The chat with the attacks lit up and every ordinary stretch folded away, a verdict in plain words for the child's age, and who is doing it (and who isn't). | | **Coach** | Don't reply, save it, block/report/mute with steps for WhatsApp, Instagram, TikTok, Snapchat and Discord, and a message to a trusted adult that Gemma drafts in a kid's voice. Ward never sends anything itself. | | **Get help now** | Anything dangerous puts helplines for the child's country first (including Pakistan's Madadgaar 1098 and DRF Cyber Harassment Helpline 0800-39393), plus Take It Down for images. | | **Evidence vault** | Saved chats are encrypted (AES-GCM, key from a PIN via PBKDF2), each message SHA-256 fingerprinted. | | **Resilience Path** | Duolingo-style daily lessons with streaks and XP: *Spot it, Shut it down, Save it, Say it, Back them up, Lock it down, Bounce back*. Content per age band (8 to 10, 11 to 13, 14 to 17). No hearts to lose. | | **Stories** | Short branching chats where *you* choose: laugh along, stay quiet, speak up, tell someone. Every ending says what that choice did and what else could work, and you can go back and try another. One for every unit in every age band (21), in English and Urdu. | | **Your night light** | Six looks the child picks from a gallery, no gender question. The age band changes how playful or grown-up it feels. | | **English and اردو** | The whole app, lessons included, in English or Urdu (right to left, Nastaliq script). Switch any time in Me. | | **Read aloud** | A Listen button on lessons, onboarding, verdicts and coach steps, on by default for the youngest children. English is narrated with ElevenLabs and bundled, so it works offline. | | **This is wrong** | A correction under every flagged message. Kept on the phone (no words), never hides the help for a dangerous message, and shared only if the child chooses. | | **Give Ward to a friend** | On Android, Ward sends itself to another phone over Bluetooth or Quick Share, no internet, with a fingerprint to check. On desktop and web, a QR code to the download (once a release is published). | | **Shared phones** | Each person gets their own Ward behind an optional PIN. Quick exit (a button, or Escape twice) locks it instantly and hides it from the recents screen. | ### The child's circle | | | | --- | --- | | **For the adult they told** | A page the child hands over, in English and Urdu: what to do in the first minutes, what not to do (take the phone away, confront the other family), and next steps with school, the app and a helpline. | | **Class mode** | A teacher projects any lesson for a whole room: one question at a time, the class votes or talks, then the answer. Ground rules up front. Nothing recorded, no accounts. | | **School kit** | A term plan, a lesson plan per unit, a letter home (English and Urdu) and an anonymous before and after survey, all printable. The teacher types in the totals and sees what changed. Nothing about any child is collected. | ### Discord | | | | --- | --- | | **Check with Ward** | Right-click any message → Apps. Is it bullying, what kind, and what to do on Discord. Only the teen sees it. Works in any server or DM, because the teen installs Ward to their own account. | | **Save as evidence** | Ward DMs the teen a fingerprinted copy. The DMs are the evidence store: the bot has no database. `/ward report` turns them into a `ward.report/v2` a counsellor can check. | | **Server mode** | Opt-in with a private `#ward-alerts` channel: dangerous messages go to moderators, the sender of a hurtful but not dangerous message gets a private nudge to edit or delete it, the target a kind check-in. Never deletes, mutes or bans. | Same engine and Ward Lite, on the CPU, no closed AI service. Self-host it in a few steps, or on Render with [`render.yaml`](render.yaml): [apps/discord/README.md](apps/discord/README.md). ### The community | | | | --- | --- | | **A helpline-ready report** | The child picks who it's for and what they want to happen; details about them are optional. They get a readable page plus `ward-report.json` in a documented format ([docs/REPORT.md](docs/REPORT.md)) with a digest a helpline can check. Only hurtful messages go in. The rest of the chat stays private. | | **Case viewer** | [`viewer/ward-viewer.html`](viewer/ward-viewer.html): one offline file a caseworker double-clicks. It checks the report against its own digest and every message's fingerprint (this catches accidental damage and casual edits, not a determined forger), puts safety and the child's wishes first, and exports a summary, a CSV or a print view. No network, nothing uploaded. | | **Counsellor mode** | A counsellor's Ward that takes a child's report by file or by QR codes from the child's screen (no internet needed), checks it, and keeps case notes. Locked with a PIN, on that device. No server. | ## Does the approach work? The scorecard Same balanced sample for every system, 200 messages per language, half abusive by each dataset's own labels. All run locally through Ollama. Method in [`eval/results/scorecard.md`](eval/results/scorecard.md); rerun with `pnpm eval`. | Caught (precision) | Word lists only | ShieldGemma 2B | **A phone: word lists + Ward Lite** | Gemma 4 E2B (phone size)\* | **A computer: Gemma 4 E4B**\* | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Roman Urdu** | 59% (94%) | 14% (70%) | **83% (86%)**† | 33% (75%) | **86% (86%)** | | **Bangla** (abuse aimed at a person) | 10% (83%) | 14% (93%) | **46% (79%)** | 34% (71%) | **65% (78%)** | | **English** (tweet dataset) | 10% (91%) | 19% (73%) | **85% (67%)**† | 33% (69%) | **36% (72%)** | † **In distribution.** For Roman Urdu and English, Ward Lite was trained on the *train* splits of the same two datasets the scorecard tests on (it never sees the test messages themselves). The other systems never saw either dataset. So these two cells show Ward Lite learned those datasets, not that a phone reads new kinds of chat better than Gemma. **Bangla is the fair comparison:** Ward Lite's Bangla came from other datasets, and there the computer's Gemma 4 E4B leads, 65% to 46%. \* **The Gemma rows are from an earlier run** and will be rerun. They were scored before Ward started asking Gemma again about messages it skipped; in that version Gemma 4 E4B left some messages without a verdict (81 of 275 on the [red-team set](docs/REDTEAM.md)), and a missing verdict counts as not caught, so these rows may undercount. **Ward Lite** is a small classifier we distilled for phones ([`train/`](train/)): 37.7 MB, about 8 ms per message on one CPU thread of the laptop that ran the scorecard, fully offline. A leak check dropped 98 training messages that also appear in the scorecard's test sets ([`train/DATA.md`](train/DATA.md)), and in the app it can only *add* warnings, never clear one. Bangla is still the weak spot: the next step is more real, non-abusive Bangla chat to train on. Catching abuse isn't enough; ordinary chat has to stay calm. A set of 329 everyday messages ("see you tomorrow", "gate pe milo, samosay"), kept out of training, is now part of the check: Ward Lite flags 5% of them, and marks 2% dangerous ([`eval/everyday`](eval/everyday)). It was written while fixing that exact problem, so read it as a development check, not a sealed test. The first release scored "see you tomorrow" as dangerous; the story is in [docs/PHASES.md](docs/PHASES.md). The [red-team set](docs/REDTEAM.md) tests disguises, sarcasm, coded slang and tricky banter, and publishes the failures. This measures whether Ward *reads* abuse, not whether children are better off. That second question needs a pilot in schools; the plan is in [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md#measurement-plan). What the numbers do and don't show: - **English is low for every system that didn't train on it.** That dataset is mostly tweets *about* gender and other topics rather than aimed at one person: word lists catch 10% and Gemma 4 E4B 36%. Ward Lite's 85% is the in-distribution case above. Ward's pattern engine is tested on the chats in [`packages/engine/fixtures`](packages/engine/fixtures). - **Small generative models are poor judges.** Gemma 3 1B cleared real insults as harmless. Gemma 4 E2B (phone-sized, run natively through LiteRT-LM) caught about a third, and it loses track of lists longer than 5 messages. So on phones Ward Lite reads the chats, and Gemma 4 E2B, if the child downloads it, does what it's good at: writing the message to a trusted adult and giving feedback on lesson answers. ## What could go wrong [`docs/HARMS.md`](docs/HARMS.md) covers false negatives, false positives, blaming the wrong person, parents using it as spyware, bullies testing messages against it, and self-harm, with what Ward does about each. None of it has been reviewed by a child-protection professional yet; that comes before any pilot. ## Why open - **Privacy is the product.** A child's chats can't go to a vendor. Open weights running locally are the only way to read them with a real language model and keep that promise. - **It works where resources are scarcest.** No account, no subscription, no data plan after install. Slang packs and patterns work on a cheap Android phone with the internet off. - **Communities own the words.** Slang packs are plain JSON (`packages/engine/packs`). The Roman Urdu pack was grown from a public dataset's training split and reviewed by hand ([`eval/mine-ru.ts`](eval/mine-ru.ts)). - **It can't disappear.** MIT licensed, and headed for the Digital Public Goods registry. ## Run it ```bash pnpm install node apps/web/scripts/copy-ort.mjs # Ward Lite's offline runtime (not in git); rerun after updating packages ollama pull gemma4:e4b # the close read; Ward still works without it pnpm dev # http://localhost:5199 pnpm test # every package, plus the viewer, corrections and red-team leak check pnpm eval # the scorecard (also needs: ollama pull shieldgemma:2b) ``` Skip the `copy-ort` step and the app still runs, but without Ward Lite, in the dev server and in every build below: where Gemma isn't set up, Ward reads with the word lists alone. - **Desktop:** `pnpm --filter @ward/desktop start`. No Ollama? Me → "Gemma inside Ward" downloads Gemma 4 once (4.6 GB) and runs it through llama.cpp inside the app. `--lab` (or the switch in Me) makes Ward forget everything on close, for shared school computers. `pnpm --filter @ward/desktop dist` builds an installer for your own computer into `release/`. GitHub Actions (`desktop.yml`) builds and launch-tests installers for macOS, Windows and Linux when run by hand; none has been published as a release yet. - **Android:** `mobile/` is a Capacitor shell with the app bundled inside and a small native plugin for Share to Ward. `pnpm --filter @ward/web build && pnpm --filter @ward/mobile apk` builds a debug APK (needs the Android SDK and JDK 21). `android.yml` builds it and launch-tests it on an emulator with Wi-Fi off. Cloud backup is off, so the vault never leaves the phone. - **Phone + family computer:** start Ollama on the computer with `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0`, then put `http://:11434` in Ward's Me screen on the phone. The phone then sends the chats it checks to that computer over your home network, unencrypted, so only do this on a network you trust. `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` lets anyone on that network use the computer's Ollama: never set it on school or public Wi-Fi. ### Opening an unsigned build Ward's installers aren't signed yet, so the first time you open one your computer warns you. - **macOS 15 and later:** open Ward once and click Done on the warning. Then open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down to Security, and click **Open Anyway** next to the line about Ward. Confirm with your password, and Ward opens. (Right-click → Open no longer skips the check on macOS 15.) If there's no Open Anyway button, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Ward.app` in Terminal, then open Ward. - **Windows:** if SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", click **More info**, then **Run anyway**. - **Linux:** make the AppImage runnable with `chmod +x Ward-linux.AppImage`, then open it. ## How it's built ``` packages/engine parser, slang packs, pattern engine, Gemma and ShieldGemma judges, the ward.report/v2 builder; unit-tested packages/lessons the Resilience Path as plain data, with content tests apps/web React 19, Vite, Tailwind 4, Motion, Phosphor icons desktop Electron, served from app://ward (one of Ollama's allowed origins) mobile Capacitor Android with the ShareIn and Give Ward plugins apps/discord the Discord bot (discord.js), same engine and Ward Lite in Node eval datasets, baselines and the scorecard docs PLAN, HARMS, SAFEGUARDING, REPORT, REDTEAM, ROADMAP, DPG ``` The drop zone's travelling rim light is adapted from the idea in cult-ui's Halo Dropzone on 21st.dev. Fonts: Bricolage Grotesque and Atkinson Hyperlegible Next. ## Help wanted If you work at a child helpline, a school, or with young people in Pakistan, India or Bangladesh, we'd like to hear what's wrong with this before anyone builds more of it. Open an issue, or start with [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md). ## Licence MIT. Helpline numbers were checked on 2026-10-29; please open an issue if one is wrong or missing for your country. { "name": "ward", "private": true, "type": "module", "packageManager": "pnpm@12.8.1", "scripts": { "dev": "pnpm --filter @ward/web dev", "build": "pnpm -r build", "typecheck": "pnpm -r typecheck", "test": "pnpm -r test && node --test --experimental-strip-types viewer/viewer.test.ts apps/web/src/lib/kitResults.test.ts apps/web/src/lib/qrTransfer.test.ts apps/web/src/lib/corrections.test.ts apps/web/src/lib/helpPaths.test.ts eval/redteam/leak.test.ts apps/web/src/lib/help.test.ts apps/web/src/lib/vaultSeal.test.ts", "eval": "node --experimental-strip-types eval/run.ts", "redteam": "node --experimental-strip-types eval/redteam/run.ts", "redteam:lite": "train/.venv/bin/python eval/redteam/score-lite.py", "secondlook": "node --experimental-strip-types eval/secondlook/run.ts gemma4:e2b gemma4:e4b" } } android.yml ci.yml desktop.yml apps: discord web packages: engine lessons

# Ward Lite training data

Built by `build-data.ts`. 28747 messages after removing duplicates, **98 that also appear in the scorecard's eval sets** and **122 that match or nearly match the everyday false-alarm set** (both dropped so those tests stay honest). 90% train, 10% dev (for choosing the checkpoint; the scorecard is separate).

## Sources

- **Roman Urdu (roman_urdu_hate_speech, train)**: 7208 rows before dedupe
- **English (Cyberbullying-Detection-CB1, train)**: 6000 rows before dedupe
- **Hinglish and Hindi (prism-hinglish-hate-speech, train)**: 6000 rows before dedupe
- **Bangla (mteb/bengali_hate_speech, personal and gender labels)**: 877 rows before dedupe
- **Bangla non-abusive (SentNoB, neutral and positive comments)**: 2500 rows before dedupe
- **Synthetic chats (Gemma 4 on this machine)**: 3743 rows before dedupe
- **Synthetic hard negatives and intent-only threats (Gemma 4 on this machine)**: 1737 rows before dedupe
- **Contrast templates (gen-contrast.ts, hand-written)**: 1160 rows before dedupe

The scorecard's own splits (Roman Urdu validation, Bangla blindspot test, CB1 test) are never used for training.

The red-team set (`eval/redteam/`, see [docs/REDTEAM.md](../docs/REDTEAM.md)) is a test set too. **Nothing in `train/` may read `eval/redteam/`**, and no red-team message may be copied or paraphrased into training data or the synthetic-data prompts. `eval/redteam/leak.test.ts`, part of `pnpm test`, fails if any red-team text turns up in `train/data` or the training scripts, or if code here opens that folder.

## Labels

- **hurtful**: the dataset's own abusive/bullying label, or the kind the synthetic message was written as.
- **danger**: threats, telling someone to hurt themselves, sexual pressure, or threats to expose. From the synthetic kind, or (for public data) a severity-3 slang-pack hit, which is a weak label.

| Language | Messages | Hurtful | Danger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ur-Latn | 8768 | 4212 | 591 |
| en | 7368 | 3829 | 613 |
| hi | 4039 | 2097 | 0 |
| hi-Latn | 3498 | 1748 | 569 |
| bn | 5074 | 1719 | 569 |

## Hard negatives and intent-only threats (added 2026-10-31)

The first Ward Lite scored "see you tomorrow" as 0.99 dangerous. The synthetic threat batches were
full of "later", "tomorrow", "after school" and "meet me", and almost nothing friendly used those
words, so the model learned the words instead of the intent. Two kinds of data fix that:

- **Friendly messages that share threat words** (hurtful 0, danger 0): goodbyes and plans ("see
  you after tuition", "kal milte hain", "কাল দেখা হবে"), caring offers ("I'll get you a samosa",
  "wait there I'm coming"), and game trash talk that names the game. Gemma 4 kinds `plans`,
  `caring`, `gaming`, plus hand-written templates in `gen-contrast.ts`.
- **Threats that rely on intent** (hurtful 1, danger 1): violence, self-harm urging, blackmail and
  sexual pressure. Gemma 4 kinds `threat-intent` and `coercion` were asked for no time or
  meeting words, and 13 that used them anyway were dropped. The templates write most
  threats with no time words and about a third starting with the same time and meeting phrases as
  the friendly templates ("see you tomorrow, I'm going to break your teeth"), so those phrases
  appear on both sides and only the intent decides.

Templates use the same names, punctuation, casing and emoji on both sides, so none of those can
become the next shortcut.

| Language | Friendly (Gemma) | Friendly (templates) | Threats (Gemma) | Threats (templates) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ur-Latn | 262 | 162 | 165 | 120 |
| en | 262 | 162 | 170 | 120 |
| hi | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| hi-Latn | 254 | 162 | 165 | 114 |
| bn | 258 | 148 | 166 | 114 |

**Held out:** the everyday false-alarm set (`eval/everyday/everyday.jsonl`, 329 friendly
messages written separately, never shown to the generators) is checked against every training
row, not only the new ones: exact match, word overlap (Jaccard >= 0.6), or containing a whole
everyday message of three or more words drops the training row. `score-everyday.py` reports how
often the exported model flags that set.

## Known weaknesses

- Public data is tweets and comments, not children's chats; synthetic chats fill that gap but were written by a model.
- Bangla non-abusive examples are SentNoB comments (neutral and positive sentiment), which are a different source from the abusive Bangla rows; the model could partly learn source style rather than abuse.
- The danger label on public data is weak (slang-pack hits only).

> **DRAFT. Not yet reviewed by a safeguarding professional, and not yet submitted.** This is a
> working draft of Ward's application to the [Digital Public Goods Alliance](https://digitalpublicgoods.net)

## About the standard

The DPG Standard has nine indicators (9 has three parts). The DPGA's GitHub repository lists the
current release as **v1.1.6** (September 2024). Its changelog adds a question about clear
ownership for content collections and data sets. The text of the indicators below is paraphrased from
the [standard](https://github.com/DPGAlliance/DPG-Standard) and the
[submission guide](https://digitalpublicgoods.net/submission-guide/), which we read on
2026-10-31. **Check both again before submitting**: the standard is revised, and the application
form at [app.digitalpublicgoods.net](https://app.digitalpublicgoods.net/signup) is the authority.

Process, from the submission guide: an optional eligibility test; gather evidence for each
indicator; an **authorised representative** of the solution submits through the DPGA application
portal; the DPGA technical review team assesses it (they aim for about 30 days); if every
requirement is met, the solution is listed on the DPG Registry, and status is renewed every year.
What is submitted becomes public under the Unlicense, except the submitter's name and contact
details.

## Summary

Ward is an offline anti-cyberbullying app for children, with the lessons, stories, school kit,
report format and viewer that go with it. It is MIT licensed and has no server and no data
collection.

| # | Indicator | Status | One line |

| ElevenLabs | Closed service | **No, at runtime** | Used once to make 107 English audio clips, which are bundled as plain MP3 files. The app makes no call to ElevenLabs. Replacements: device text-to-speech (already used for Urdu) or any open TTS. |
| Android and Capacitor, Electron | Open source frameworks | Yes, for each shell | The web app also runs in a browser. A fork could use any shell. |
| Google Play, App Store | Closed distribution | No | Ward is distributed as an APK and desktop installers on GitHub. F-Droid is planned. |
| Operating systems (Android, macOS, Windows, Linux) | Mixed | Not controlled by us | Normal for apps. |

The test is whether the core product works without the closed parts. It does: the word lists,
patterns, lessons, stories, vault, report and viewer need none of them.

**Evidence.** [README.md](../README.md#how-its-built), [PHASES.md](PHASES.md#partner-technologies)
(which lists what each partner technology is for and what is "not used, on purpose"),
`packages/engine/package.json`, `apps/web/package.json`.

**Gap.** A written statement, by someone technical, on Gemma's licence and on the
ElevenLabs-generated audio. Also, a few partner services in PHASES.md are "planned" (DigitalOcean,
Render, Browserbase, SerpApi) and must be kept optional if they are adopted.

**Status: partly met.**

### 5. Documentation

**Requirement.** For software: technical documentation that lets an unfamiliar technical person
launch and run it. For content collections: usage instructions and compatible apps. For data
projects: describe the fields, how the data was collected and how to interpret it.

**Ward.**
- **Run and build:** the "Run it" section of [README.md](../README.md#run-it) (install, dev
  server, tests, scorecard, desktop and Android builds).
- **Architecture:** [PLAN.md](PLAN.md) (layout, platforms, scope cuts) and the README's
  [How it's built](../README.md#how-its-built).
- **Use cases and requirements:** [PLAN.md](PLAN.md), [PHASES.md](PHASES.md),
  [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).
- **Risks:** [HARMS.md](HARMS.md).
- **Data formats:** [REPORT.md](REPORT.md) documents `ward.report/v2` field by field, including
  how to verify the digest by hand.
- **Training data:** [`train/DATA.md`](../train/DATA.md) lists sources, split, counts, labels and
  known weaknesses; [`train/README.md`](../train/README.md) covers the pipeline.
- **Evaluation:** [`eval/results/scorecard.md`](../eval/results/scorecard.md) and
  `pnpm eval`.
- **Slang packs:** each pack states its source in its `about` field.
- **Tests and CI:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs typecheck, tests and a build on every push to
  `main` and every pull request; `desktop.yml` and `android.yml` build and launch-test the
  installers and the APK when run by hand or on a version tag. No release has been tagged yet.

**Gaps.**
- No `CONTRIBUTING.md`, no guide for adding a slang pack or a language, and no guide for
  translating lessons. (A language-maintainer guide is implied by [GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md).)
- No step-by-step release or signing guide for the desktop and Android builds.
- No end-user manual beyond the in-app text.
- No documented learning outcomes for the lessons.

**Status: partly met.**

### 6. Mechanism for extracting data and content

**Requirement.** For systems without PII, export or import of non-PII data and content in a
non-proprietary format.

**Ward.** Ward has no server and holds no PII on any server. Content and exports use open formats:

- **Slang packs, lessons and stories** are plain JSON in the repository (`packages/engine/packs`,
  `packages/lessons/src`). They can be read, edited and reused directly.
- **Reports** are produced as `ward-report.json` (a documented, versioned schema) and a
  readable HTML page ([REPORT.md](REPORT.md)).
- **The case viewer** exports a plain-text summary, a CSV (with spreadsheet formulas
  neutralised) and a print view.
- **The school kit** lets a teacher download class totals as CSV. Nothing about any child is in
  them.
- **The scorecard** is published as Markdown and JSON.
- **Chat input** is a standard WhatsApp text export, pasted text or an image.

What a child saves in the vault is personal data and is encrypted on their device. It is
deliberately not exportable in bulk; the child can make a report from it. This is by design and
consistent with the indicator, which is about non-PII data.

**Evidence.** [REPORT.md](REPORT.md), `viewer/ward-viewer.html`, `eval/results/scorecard.json`,
`packages/lessons/src`.

**Status: met.**

### 7. Adherence to privacy and applicable laws

**Requirement.** Show the good is designed and developed to comply with privacy and other
applicable laws. The evidence must come from someone authorised to speak for the project, with
their title, name and contact information. The submission guide asks, if personal data is
collected, for a link to the privacy policy or terms, and encourages listing the laws that
apply.

**Ward.** By design, Ward collects no personal data: no account, no server of ours, no
analytics, no telemetry. A child's chats are read on the device and forgotten unless saved, and
saved evidence is encrypted. There are two exceptions, each chosen by whoever sets it up:

- **A paired phone.** A phone can be paired with the family's own computer running Ollama, and
  then the chats it checks are sent to that computer, over the home network and unencrypted, to
  be read there.
- **The optional Discord bot** (`apps/discord`) runs on a computer its operator hosts. In server
  mode (on unless the operator turns it off) it receives the messages of the servers it is added
  to, reads them in any server with a `#ward-alerts` channel, and posts dangerous ones, quoted,
  to that private moderators' channel. If the operator sets `WARD_GEMMA_MODEL`, a message only
  Ward Lite flagged is also sent to the operator's Ollama for a second look, with the messages
  just before it.

Nothing goes to the project in either case. Collecting nothing is the strongest privacy position
available, and it is described in [README.md](../README.md), [HARMS.md](HARMS.md) and
[SAFEGUARDING.md](SAFEGUARDING.md).

**What is missing.**
- **No privacy policy or terms of use** document. Even an app that collects nothing should say
  so, in plain language for a child and in full for an adult. `[Decision needed: write
  docs/PRIVACY.md; have a lawyer check it.]`
- **No legal review.** The laws that may apply depend on where the app is used. The ones to
  assess include, at least: the EU General Data Protection Regulation (including rules on
  children's consent), the UK Children's Code (Age Appropriate Design Code), the US Children's
  Online Privacy Protection Act, and Pakistan's, India's and Bangladesh's data-protection and
  cyber-crime laws. `[Decision needed: obtain a legal opinion for the countries Ward is aimed
  at. Do not assert compliance with any law until a lawyer has said so.]`
- **No statement from an authorised person**, which the indicator requires. `[Authorised
  representative: name, title and contact to be supplied.]`
- Some network calls exist: the optional Ollama computer (which receives the chats it is asked
  to read, as above), the optional model download and helpline links (which carry no chat), and
  the Discord bot, which talks to Discord and, if set up, to its operator's Ollama (as above). A
  privacy policy must describe all of them, and the bot's operator is responsible for the
  messages it reads on their server.

**Status: not yet met.** The design supports it; the paperwork does not exist. This indicator
needs work before submission.

### 8. Adherence to standards and best practices

**Requirement.** Designed and developed in line with relevant standards, best practices and
principles.

**Ward.**
- **Open standards and formats:** AES-GCM, PBKDF2 and SHA-256 for the vault and report integrity
  (via the Web Crypto API); ISO 8601 times; JSON; ONNX for the model; UTF-8 text; QR codes;
  standard WhatsApp exports.
- **Engineering practice:** TypeScript with strict typechecking, unit tests (engine, lessons,
  stories, report, viewer, school kit, QR transfer), CI on every push, installers built and
  launch-tested in CI, a permission handler in the desktop app that refuses everything but the
  camera, and a case viewer whose content-security policy blocks every network request. The web
  and desktop app themselves have no content-security policy yet.
- **Privacy by design and data minimisation:** the "never do" list in
  [SAFEGUARDING.md](SAFEGUARDING.md#8-what-ward-will-never-do), reflecting practice in the UN
  Convention on the Rights of the Child (the child's best interests and right to privacy).
- **Accessibility and inclusion:** an accessibility-first typeface (Atkinson Hyperlegible Next),
  right-to-left Urdu in a Nastaliq font, read-aloud, a gender-neutral design, low-resource
  hardware targets, and an offline-first approach.
- **Evidence-informed:** the roadmap cites the intervention research
  ([ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md#sources)) and treats it honestly, including that app-only
  interventions have thin evidence.
- **Open source practice:** a public changelog in git, issues, a code of conduct and a security
  policy (drafts).

**Gaps, stated plainly.**
- No accessibility audit against WCAG, or against a mobile accessibility standard. `[Planned.]`
- No independent security review or penetration test. `[Planned.]`
- No mapping to a child-safety framework (for example the UK Children's Code, UNICEF's guidance
  on children and AI, or a national standard). `[Planned.]`
- Safe-messaging guidance for suicide and self-harm content is not yet named or checked by a
  qualified person ([SAFEGUARDING.md](SAFEGUARDING.md#5-how-content-is-written-and-reviewed)).
- No content review by a child-protection professional yet.
- Ward Annotate (community labelling), which would strengthen best practice on model
  evaluation, is not yet built ([PHASES.md](PHASES.md#phase-5-proof-and-staying-alive)). The
  red-team set is built and its failures are published ([REDTEAM.md](REDTEAM.md)); its labels are
  still one author's, with no native-speaker review.
- No content-security policy in the web and desktop app, and Electron's hardening fuses are not
  set. `[Planned.]`

**Status: partly met.**

### 9. Do no harm by design

**Requirement.** Show the good is designed to anticipate, prevent and avoid harm. It has three
parts, each of which applies if the system does the thing named.

#### 9a. Data privacy and security

**Requirement.** For systems that collect, store or distribute PII, show how privacy, security
and integrity are ensured.

**Ward.** The project collects, stores and distributes no PII. On the child's own device:

- the vault is AES-GCM encrypted with a key from a PIN (PBKDF2, 310,000 rounds); the PIN is not
  stored; the safety plan, case notes and evidence share that seal;
- each person on a shared phone has their own database, an optional PIN, and a quick exit that
  locks Ward at once, hides it from the recents screen on Android (`FLAG_SECURE`) and, on
  desktop, can be triggered by pressing Escape twice;
- Android cloud backup is off (`android:allowBackup="false"`);
- the desktop app refuses every permission except the camera for scanning;
- reports carry a SHA-256 digest and a per-message fingerprint. These catch accidental damage
  and casual edits; they are unkeyed, so they don't stop a determined forger who recomputes them
  ([REPORT.md](REPORT.md#checking-a-report)).

[HARMS.md](HARMS.md) lists what can go wrong with Ward's own data and what we do about it,
including that a short PIN can be brute-forced by a determined person with the device.
[SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md) describes how to report a flaw privately.

**Gaps.** No independent security review. Android allows cleartext traffic so the phone can reach
a family computer's Ollama; this is documented in [SECURITY.md](../SECURITY.md) and should be
tightened.

**Status: met, self-assessed.** The honest wording for the application is "collects no PII; the
protections for the data on the device are documented but have not been independently audited."

#### 9b. Inappropriate and illegal content

**Requirement.** For systems that collect, store or distribute content, have policies that
identify inappropriate and illegal content (such as child sexual abuse material) and processes
to detect, moderate, report and remove it.

**Ward.** Ward does not collect or distribute user content. The app handles messages only on the
device. The project does host a public repository, which accepts issues and pull requests. It
also contains slang packs and test fixtures that include abusive words. Where it applies:

- [SAFEGUARDING.md](SAFEGUARDING.md#7-disclosures-and-concerns-that-reach-the-project) says what
  to do when someone posts a real child's chat, a disclosure, or child sexual abuse material:
  do not open it, report it to the national hotline and GitHub, remove it from view, tell the
  safeguarding lead.
- [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](../CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) forbids putting a real child's data into the
  project.
- The ways the app can contain harmful content of its own are covered by content rules, a review
  process and the models' limits in [SAFEGUARDING.md](SAFEGUARDING.md#5-how-content-is-written-and-reviewed).

**Gaps.** These are drafts, not published and not reviewed. No issue templates yet warn people
not to paste real chats. No named safeguarding lead to act on a report. No tested process.

**Status: partly met.**

#### 9c. Protection from harassment

**Requirement.** If the good enables interaction between users or contributors, have a process
for protecting them from griefing, abuse and harassment, and systems addressing the safety and
security of underage users.

**Ward.** The app has no chat, messaging or social feature between users, so there is nothing for
users to harass each other with. Contributors interact in the repository, and young people may
take part in a future advisory group and in Ward Annotate. Underage users' safety is the reason
Ward exists. What we have drafted:

- [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](../CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md): the Contributor Covenant 2.1 plus rules for
  a project that serves children, with a private reporting route.
- [SAFEGUARDING.md](SAFEGUARDING.md): the policy, including the checks for adults who work with
  young people and the "never do" list.
- [GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md): the safeguarding lead role, the safeguarding veto, and the
  protections for the youth advisory group.
- In the app, age bands, shared-phone profiles with a quick exit, and a danger path that puts
  helplines first ([SAFEGUARDING.md](SAFEGUARDING.md#4-what-ward-does-when-it-sees-danger)).

**Gaps.** The safeguarding lead is not appointed. No one has done a background check. The youth
advisory group does not exist. None of the documents has been reviewed by a qualified person.

**Status: partly met.**

## What to do before submitting

In order of how much they block the application:

1. Appoint the safeguarding lead and have the safeguarding documents reviewed; publish them.
2. Write a privacy policy; get a legal read for the countries Ward is aimed at; name the
   authorised representative (indicator 7, and the submitter role).
3. Settle licensing: content licence, audio, the Gemma and Ward Lite models, training-data
   licences (indicator 2, 4).
4. Add `CONTRIBUTING.md`, a trademark and name statement, and a plain statement of ownership
   (indicator 3, 5).
5. Switch on GitHub private vulnerability reporting; add issue templates (9b).
6. Run the eligibility test on the DPGA site, then re-read the current standard and form.
7. Fill in the online application using this document as source material. Keep the answers
   public-safe: the DPGA publishes them.

- Trademark search and name policy.
- Whether and where to host the repository in an organisation.
- Which laws apply, and a legal reviewer.
- Mirroring the optional phone model.

# Ward red-team set

Messages written to slip past Ward (disguised insults, coded slang, sarcasm, polite exclusion, indirect threats) and harmless look-alikes written to trip it (banter between friends, reclaimed words, a child quoting abuse to ask for help, game trash talk), in every language Ward reads. Rerun on every release next to the [scorecard](../eval/results/scorecard.md). Failures are published on purpose: they say where Ward is weak today.

Last run: 2026-10-31. Regenerate with `pnpm redteam:lite && pnpm redteam` (add `-- --gemma` with Ollama running). Everything below except "What fails, and why" is written by the runner, [eval/redteam/run.ts](../eval/redteam/run.ts); every miss and false alarm is in [eval/results/redteam.md](../eval/results/redteam.md).

## Method

- **The set.** 275 short messages in [eval/redteam/](../eval/redteam/), one JSONL file per language, written by hand for this purpose. All synthetic: no real children's messages, no scraped chats. Each has the engine's severity (0 harmless, 1 rude, 2 bullying, 3 dangerous), its category, the trick it tests and a note. Self-harm and sexual items stay non-graphic (no methods; image pressure only as "send pics"). The Roman Urdu, Hinglish and Bangla items still need review by native speakers of each; labels are one author's judgement.
- **Never trained on.** `eval/redteam/leak.test.ts` (part of `pnpm test`) fails if any red-team text is in Ward Lite's training data (`train/data`, when present) or its scripts, and if any code in `train/` opens this folder. See [train/DATA.md](../train/DATA.md).
- **Not tuned against.** Word lists and Ward Lite were not changed to pass this set. A fix should come from new, different examples or pack entries justified on their own, and the set should gain new items after each fix, or these numbers stop meaning anything.
- **Scoring, as in the scorecard.** A message counts as flagged when the system calls it hurtful at all: any word-list hit of severity 1 or more, Ward Lite over its threshold. *Caught* is the share of hurtful messages flagged; *false alarms* is the share of harmless look-alikes flagged; *dangerous* is the share of severity-3 messages marked dangerous (a severity-3 word-list hit, or Ward Lite's danger output). Each message is read alone, without the chat around it, which is harder than what Ward sees in a real chat.
- **Small numbers.** A language has 14 to 36 messages on each side and a language-and-trick cell as few as 2: read them as where to look, not as rates.
- **Each system alone.** As in the scorecard, the Gemma row is Gemma by itself. In the app, the computer tier also keeps a severity-3 word-list hit visible (at severity 2) when Gemma reads it as a joke.

- **Slang packs**: Ward's word lists alone: no model, works on any phone.

1. **A child asking for help reads as the bully.** When a child quotes what was said to them ("someone told me to kys and i can't stop thinking about it", "kisi ne mujhe kaha mar jao, mujhe dar lag raha hai", "কেউ আমাকে বলেছে মরে যা, আমার ভয় লাগছে"), the phone flags 10 of 14, and all 5 that quote a self-harm phrase are marked *dangerous* by the word lists. In a group chat this is the message where a child tells friends what happened.
2. **Indirect danger in South Asian languages.** "We know where you live" is missed in Roman Urdu, Bangla script and romanised Bangla; "meet me at the gate (or outside) after school, then I'll show you" in Roman Urdu, Hinglish and Bangla script; "everyone would be happier without you" in all four South Asian sets. 3. **Sarcasm and backhanded compliments get through.** Word lists 0 of 21, phone 3 of 21, Gemma 9 of 21. "omg congrats on finally getting a friend, so proud of you 🥹", "waah, aaj to tum insaan lag rahi ho 🙂", "বাহ, আজকে তো তোকে মানুষের মতো লাগছে 🙂" pass every phone layer.

That is the known limit of the packs layer, and the reason only Gemma may clear a hit; it flagged 7 of the 14 banter messages.
5. **Bangla in Bangla script.** Ward Lite catches 5 of 21 hurtful Bangla-script messages at its 0.48 threshold, against 9 of 19 for the same kinds of message in romanised Bangla. It agrees with the scorecard's weak Bangla and the data card's warning about where the Bangla negatives come from. Gemma skipped 24 of the 41 Bangla-script messages in its run (see Systems).

# Ward Lite

A small multilingual classifier that reads chat messages on any device, including cheap phones
with no internet. It's `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small` fine-tuned with two outputs per message,
**hurtful** and **danger** (threats, telling someone to hurt themselves, sexual pressure, threats
to expose), then trimmed to the vocabulary our languages use and quantised to int8 ONNX.

In the app it has **raise-only** authority: it can flag what the word lists missed, but it can
never clear a warning. Only Gemma 4 on a computer may decide that rude words between friends
were banter.

## Reproduce it

```bash
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv && uv pip install --python .venv -r pyproject.toml pyarrow
.venv/bin/python fetch.py                          # public train splits, as parquet
ollama pull gemma4:e4b
node --experimental-strip-types gen-synthetic.ts   # kid-style chats written by Gemma 4 (resumable)
node --experimental-strip-types gen-contrast.ts    # hand-written contrast pairs: friendly plans vs threats
ollama stop gemma4:e4b                             # free the memory before training
node --experimental-strip-types build-data.ts      # dedupe + leak checks (scorecard, everyday set)
.venv/bin/python train.py                          # fine-tune, trim, export to apps/web/public/models
.venv/bin/python calibrate.py                      # per-script hurtful thresholds + danger threshold, on dev
.venv/bin/python score.py                          # run the exported model on the scorecard sample
.venv/bin/python score-everyday.py                 # false alarms on everyday friendly chat (held out)
cd .. && pnpm eval -- --only="Ward Lite,Phone: packs + Ward Lite"
```

`build-data.ts` refuses to run until `pnpm eval` has cached the scorecard's eval sets, because it
needs them to drop any training message the scorecard tests on. The data card is
[DATA.md](DATA.md).

Training takes minutes on an Apple M-series laptop (PyTorch on MPS). Don't run it while Ollama
has Gemma loaded on a 16 GB machine; they compete for the same memory.

The steward is currently the only maintainer. That is a risk, and we name it. The first goal of
this document is to make it possible for someone else to become one.

## How decisions are made

**Small changes** (a typo, a bug fix, a test) are merged by any maintainer after one review. If
there is only one maintainer, they say what they checked in the pull request.

**Anything that changes what a child sees, types or shares** needs more. This includes lesson
and story text, coach steps, verdict wording, helplines, slang pack entries, prompts sent to
Gemma, and any new permission. These need:

1. a maintainer's approval, **and**
2. the language maintainer's approval if the change is in or for a language they own, **and**
3. the safeguarding lead's approval if it touches danger, self-harm, sexual content, telling an
   adult, the safety plan, or any gated feature.

**Larger decisions** (a new feature, a new platform, a new language, a dependency that changes
what the app can do, a change to the licence or to this document) are proposed in a public issue
labelled `proposal`. The discussion stays open for at least **7 days**. Maintainers decide by
**lazy consensus**: if no maintainer objects, the proposal passes. If a maintainer objects, we
talk until we reach agreement; if we cannot, a majority of maintainers decides, and the steward
breaks a tie.

**Things nobody can vote through.** These need the safeguarding lead's written agreement, a
public issue open for at least 30 days, and an announcement in the README:

- anything that makes Ward collect, send or share a child's data;
- anything that contacts anyone on the child's behalf;
- any adult-facing view of a child's chats or checks;
- turning on a gated feature (quiet mode, the keyboard);
- weakening the commitments in [SAFEGUARDING.md](SAFEGUARDING.md#8-what-ward-will-never-do).

**Safeguarding veto.** The safeguarding lead can block a release or revert a change that puts a
child at risk. The veto is recorded publicly with the reason, unless the reason would identify a
child (in which case the existence of the veto is public and the reason is recorded privately).

**Conflicts of interest.** Anyone who reviews a change must say if they have a financial,
employment or personal interest in it. Anyone with a conflict steps out of that decision.
Funders and partners (see [PHASES.md](PHASES.md#partner-technologies)) can ask for things;
they cannot decide what the app does with a child's data.

## Becoming a maintainer

There is no seniority test. We look for people who have shown care and judgement.

1. Contribute over a period of at least **three months**, with a few accepted pull requests that
   include tests.
2. Read [SAFEGUARDING.md](SAFEGUARDING.md) and [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md), and say
   so.
3. Be nominated by an existing maintainer (or nominate yourself in a `proposal` issue).
4. No maintainer objects within 7 days.

A maintainer who has been inactive for **six months** is moved to "emeritus" after a message
asking whether they want to stay. Emeritus maintainers can return by asking. A maintainer can be
removed for a serious breach of the code of conduct or safeguarding policy by agreement of the
other maintainers and the safeguarding lead.

## Language maintainers

Ward is only useful in a language if the people who speak it say it is. Today, Ward has slang
packs for English, Roman Urdu, Hinglish and Bangla, and an interface and lessons in English and
Urdu. None of those has a named language maintainer yet. The Roman Urdu pack was grown from a
public dataset and reviewed by hand, but not under any process described here, and the Urdu
text is still waiting for a native speaker's review ([PHASES.md](PHASES.md)).

**What a language maintainer owns**, for one language (or one script of a language):

- **The slang pack** (`packages/engine/packs/<lang>.json`): which words and phrases are in it,
  with what meaning, category and severity. Two people review every added word: the proposer and
  the maintainer.
- **Translations**: the interface strings (`apps/web/src/i18n`), the lessons and stories, the
  coach steps, the adult guide and the school kit, and their tone and register for each age band.
- **Lesson review**: reading content in that language for meaning, for words that carry an
  unintended meaning, for cultural fit, and for anything that could shame a child.
- **The language's scorecard line**: keeping the test data honest, writing red-team cases in that
  language, and helping publish where Ward fails in it. Weak spots stay public. Bangla is one
  today.
- **Helpline entries** for countries where that language is spoken, with cited sources.

**What a language maintainer does not own:** the engine, the safeguarding policy, or the
"never do" list. They can say a change in their language is wrong; they cannot approve changes
to the app's data handling.

**How someone becomes one:**

1. They speak and write the language natively or at near-native level, and know how children
   and teenagers actually write it in chat.
2. They have contributed or reviewed in that language (a pack, a translation, a review of an
   existing lesson), in public, over at least a few weeks.
3. They read the safeguarding policy and code of conduct.
4. An existing maintainer or language maintainer nominates them in a `proposal` issue; 7 days
   with no objection.
5. They are listed in `MAINTAINERS.md` **(planned, to be created when the first one is
   confirmed)** with the name or handle they choose.

New languages: the first volunteer who meets the above and has a second person willing to review
becomes the maintainer for it, and the language gets its own folder and entry in the pack
list. A language with no active maintainer for six months is marked "unmaintained" in the README,
and its pack and text stay readable but are flagged as not recently reviewed.

Language maintainers who are under 18 are welcome as contributors, not as maintainers, and may
join the youth advisory group instead.
## 5. How content is written and reviewed

"Content" means lessons, stories, coach steps, verdict wording, the adult guide, the school kit,
helpline entries, slang packs and Gemma's instructions.

**Rules for everything a child reads** (the first two are already enforced by tests):

- No em dashes in anything a child reads.
- The Urdu lessons must match the English ones in structure, lesson by lesson and exercise by
  exercise.
- Writing is never marked wrong. Gemma's feedback is one warm, specific note; without a model the
  child sees an example answer.
- No shaming, no guilt, no streak pressure, no hearts to lose.
- Stories and lessons never show a real person's name, a real school or a real platform's
  private details. Characters are the shared cast.
- Do not quote slurs in a lesson or story when a description will do. Where an example message is
  needed, use the mildest one that teaches the point.
- Nothing that teaches a way to harm oneself or another person, or that could work as a how-to
  for stalking, unmasking or evading a platform's safety tools.
- Anything about suicide or self-harm follows recognised safe-messaging guidance and points to a
  helpline. **Planned:** name the guidance we follow and have the reviewer check it.

**Review before release.** Today, content is reviewed by the maintainer who wrote it and by the
automated tests. That is not enough for material about bullying, self-harm and sexual pressure.
The intended process, which is **planned**:

1. **Draft** by anyone, through a pull request.
2. **Language review** by the language maintainer for that language (see
   [GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md#language-maintainers)): is the wording natural, is it the right
   register for the age band, is it free of unintended meanings?
3. **Safeguarding review** by the safeguarding lead or a delegated qualified reviewer, for
   anything that touches danger, self-harm, sexual content, telling an adult, or the safety plan.
4. **Young people's review** by the youth advisory group where it exists: does this sound like
   it was written by someone who has met a teenager?
5. **Record.** The pull request notes who reviewed what. Reviewers' names appear only with their
   consent.

**Not to be turned on more widely until the professional review is done:** the safety plan, the
"Was I mean?" repair steps, and every crisis path. All three are in the app today, unreviewed:
treat them as previews, and do not promote them to children more widely (in a campaign, a
school roll-out or a store listing) until the review is done. The phases document already says
this for the safety plan.

**Slang packs** are plain JSON, so anyone can propose a word. A word may only be added with its
meaning, a severity and a note on why it is there. **Planned:** two-person review on every added
word, one of them the language maintainer, and a published list of what each word means.

**Gemma and other models.** Models only read, draft and give feedback. Ward Lite can only raise
a warning. Gemma can clear a word-list hit it reads as harmless. A dangerous one it cannot clear,
but it can lower it to hurtful, and then that message alone no longer brings up "Get help now"
or the help block ([section 4](#4-what-ward-does-when-it-sees-danger), item 4). When
Gemma takes a second look at a message only Ward Lite flagged, it can clear a hurtful flag, but a
dangerous one it can at most mark as unsure, never clear. Models cannot send anything and cannot
reach the network except the child's own Ollama computer. Prompts sent to a model are in the open
source code and are part of content review. Model output is shown to the child as a suggestion
they can edit or ignore.

# Contributing to Ward

Thank you for helping. Ward is for children who are being hurt online, so a few rules here are
stricter than in most projects. Please read this page, the [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
and the [safeguarding policy](docs/SAFEGUARDING.md) before you open a pull request.

## The one rule that matters most

**Never paste a real child's chat, name, photo, school or phone number anywhere in this project:**
not in an issue, a pull request, a test fixture, a commit message or a discussion. Not even your
own child's, and not even with names removed. Write a made-up message that shows the same thing.
If you see real data here, don't open or share it; follow
[SAFEGUARDING.md section 7](docs/SAFEGUARDING.md#7-disclosures-and-concerns-that-reach-the-project).

If a child is in danger right now, contact your local emergency number or a child helpline
([findahelpline.com](https://findahelpline.com)) first. An issue here is not watched around the clock.

## Ways to help

| You can | Start with |
| --- | --- |
| Report a wrong or missing helpline number | The **Helpline update** issue form |
| Suggest a slang word Ward should know | The **Slang word** issue form |
| Report a false alarm (Ward flagged something friendly) | The **False alarm** issue form |
| Translate or review a translation | The **Translation** issue form and [LANGUAGES.md](LANGUAGES.md) |
| Report a bug | The **Bug** issue form |
| Report a security flaw | **Not an issue.** Follow [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) |
| Raise a safeguarding concern | **Not an issue.** Follow [SAFEGUARDING.md section 10](docs/SAFEGUARDING.md#10-raising-a-concern-about-the-project-itself) |
| Propose a bigger change (a feature, a language, a platform) | A plain issue titled "Proposal: ...", open for at least 7 days ([GOVERNANCE.md](docs/GOVERNANCE.md#how-decisions-are-made)) |

Good first tasks are drafted in [docs/SEED_ISSUES.md](docs/SEED_ISSUES.md).

## Sign your commits (DCO)

Ward uses the [Developer Certificate of Origin](https://developercertificate.org) instead of a
contributor licence agreement. By signing off a commit you say you wrote it, or have the right to
submit it, under the project's licence. You keep your copyright.

Add the sign-off with `-s`:

```bash
git commit -s -m "Add Bangla word for 'fat' with a note"
```

That adds a line like `Signed-off-by: Your Name <you@example.com>` to the commit. Use a name and
email you are happy to have public. Every commit in a pull request needs one. If you forgot,
`git commit --amend -s` fixes the last commit and `git rebase --signoff main` fixes them all.

Today the sign-off is checked by hand when a pull request is reviewed; there is no automatic
check yet.

**Licence of contributions.** Code is MIT, like the rest of the repository ([LICENSE](LICENSE)).
The licence for lessons, stories, the school kit and translations has not been decided yet (see
[docs/DPG.md](docs/DPG.md#2-use-of-approved-open-licences)); until it is, they are contributed
under the repository's MIT licence.

## Set up and run the tests

You need Node 24 and pnpm (the version is pinned in `package.json`).

```bash
pnpm install
node apps/web/scripts/copy-ort.mjs   # Ward Lite's offline runtime; optional for most changes
pnpm dev                             # the app at http://localhost:5199
pnpm -r typecheck
pnpm test
```

`pnpm test` runs every package's tests (engine, lessons, web, Discord bot) plus the viewer,
school kit, QR transfer, corrections, help paths, vault and red-team leak tests. CI runs the
same command, a typecheck and a web build on every pull request
([`.github/workflows/ci.yml`](.github/workflows/ci.yml)). Please run both before you push.

Ollama and Gemma are only needed if you work on the "close read" or run the scorecard
(`pnpm eval`). Most changes don't need them.

## Pull requests

- One change per pull request, with a short plain description of what changed and why.
- Add or update a test when you change behaviour.
- Say what you checked. If you couldn't test something (say, on Android), say that.
- Use made-up messages in tests and fixtures. The shared cast of characters in the stories is a
  good source of names.
- Small changes (a typo, a bug fix, a test) are merged after one maintainer review. Anything that
  changes what a child sees, types or shares needs more: see below and
  [GOVERNANCE.md](docs/GOVERNANCE.md#how-decisions-are-made).

## How slang-pack changes are reviewed

Slang packs are plain JSON in [`packages/engine/packs/`](packages/engine/packs/), one file per
language or script. Each entry is:

```json
{ "t": "the word or phrase, written the most common way", "c": "insult", "s": 1, "g": "English meaning" }
```

- `c` is one of `insult`, `appearance`, `identity`, `exclusion`, `threat`, `selfharm`, `sexual`,
  `exposure`, `mockery`.
- `s` is severity: **1** rude, **2** bullying, **3** dangerous. Severity 3 puts helplines first
  in the app, so it needs the most care.

A new word needs its meaning, a category, a severity, and a note in the pull request on why it is
there and where children use it. Then:

1. **Two people review it**: the proposer and a second speaker of the language. Once a language
   has a [language maintainer](LANGUAGES.md), that second person is the maintainer. Today no
   language has one, so the steward reviews and asks for a second speaker in the issue.
2. **Check for false alarms.** Many insults are also everyday words ("pagal" between friends,
   "kala" as a colour). Say how the word is used kindly, if it is. The engine tests include
   everyday Roman Urdu and English that must not trip the packs; add a line there if your word
   has an innocent twin.
3. **Severity 3 and anything sexual or about self-harm** also needs the safeguarding lead
   ([SAFEGUARDING.md section 5](docs/SAFEGUARDING.md#5-how-content-is-written-and-reviewed)). That
   role is not filled yet, so these words wait.
4. **Never tune to the test sets.** Don't add a word because it fixes a miss in
   [docs/REDTEAM.md](docs/REDTEAM.md) or the scorecard. A word has to be justified on its own,
   with an example you wrote yourself, or those numbers stop meaning anything.
5. `pnpm test` must pass.

## How lesson and story changes are reviewed

Lessons and stories live in [`packages/lessons/src/`](packages/lessons/src/) (`units.ts` and
`stories.ts` in English, `units.ur.ts` and `stories.ur.ts` in Urdu). The interface text is in
[`apps/web/src/i18n/`](apps/web/src/i18n/).

The tests already enforce two rules: no em dashes in anything a child reads, and the Urdu lessons
match the English ones exercise by exercise. So a change to an English lesson needs the Urdu one
changed in the same pull request (or a note asking for a translator, and the pull request waits).

The rest of the rules are in
[SAFEGUARDING.md section 5](docs/SAFEGUARDING.md#5-how-content-is-written-and-reviewed): no
shaming, no streak pressure, the mildest example that teaches the point, no real names, schools
or platforms' private details, and safe-messaging for anything about self-harm. Review is:

1. a maintainer;
2. a speaker of each language changed (the language maintainer, once there is one);
3. the safeguarding lead for anything that touches danger, self-harm, sexual content, telling an
   adult or the safety plan.

Until the safeguarding lead is appointed, changes in step 3 can be merged as drafts only if the
pull request says so plainly. They are not to be promoted to children more widely.

## Helpline numbers

Helplines are in [`apps/web/src/lib/help.ts`](apps/web/src/lib/help.ts). Every change must cite
where the number came from (the service's own site, Child Helpline International, or a
government page) in the pull request, and the date you checked it. Don't add a number you only
found on a list site. If a line is not free to call or has limited hours, say so in its note.

## Training data and Ward Lite

See [`train/README.md`](train/README.md), the data card [`train/DATA.md`](train/DATA.md) and the
model card [`train/MODEL_CARD.md`](train/MODEL_CARD.md). Nothing in `train/` may read
`eval/redteam/`, and a test fails if it does.

## Questions

Open an issue. Please be patient: Ward is maintained by one person today
([GOVERNANCE.md](docs/GOVERNANCE.md#roles)).

# Languages in Ward

Ward is only useful in a language if the people who speak it say it is. This page lists what
exists in each language and script, and who looks after it.

**Today nobody does.** No language has a named language maintainer. Everything below was written
or assembled by the project's one maintainer, and none of the South Asian language work has been
reviewed by a native speaker under the process in
[GOVERNANCE.md](docs/GOVERNANCE.md#language-maintainers). Read every line here as unreviewed.

## What exists

| Language or script | Slang pack | App and lessons | Read aloud | Ward Lite training data | Red-team items | Maintainer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| English | [`en.json`](packages/engine/packs/en.json), 53 entries | Yes | Bundled recordings | Yes (tweets, CB1) | 71 | **None** |
| Urdu (Urdu script) | None: packs never match Urdu script | Yes, right to left, Nastaliq | Device voice, not tested on every phone | None | None | **None** |
| Roman Urdu | [`ur-Latn.json`](packages/engine/packs/ur-Latn.json), 117 entries | No (Roman Urdu speakers use the Urdu or English app) | No | Yes (roman_urdu_hate_speech) | 67 | **None** |
| Hinglish (Hindi in Latin letters) | [`hi-Latn.json`](packages/engine/packs/hi-Latn.json), 19 entries | No | No | Yes | 63 | **None** |
| Hindi (Devanagari) | None | No | No | Yes, but no danger examples | None | **None** |
| Bangla (Bangla script) | [`bn.json`](packages/engine/packs/bn.json), 30 entries shared with romanised Bangla | No | No | Yes | 41 | **None** |
| Bangla (romanised) | Shares `bn.json` | No | No | Some, in the synthetic chats | 33 | **None** |

Entry counts are as of 2026-10-31; the files are the source of truth. Red-team counts are from
[docs/REDTEAM.md](docs/REDTEAM.md). How well Ward reads each language is in the
[scorecard](eval/results/scorecard.md) and [docs/REDTEAM.md](docs/REDTEAM.md); Bangla and Urdu
script are the weakest.

## What a language maintainer does

In short (the full description is in
[GOVERNANCE.md](docs/GOVERNANCE.md#language-maintainers)):

- owns the slang pack for one language or script, and is the second reviewer on every added word;
- reviews translations of the interface, lessons, stories, adult guide and school kit for meaning,
  register and anything that could shame a child;
- keeps that language's scorecard line and red-team items honest, and helps publish failures;
- checks helpline entries for countries where the language is spoken.

They don't own the engine, the safeguarding policy or the "never do" list.

## Becoming one

You speak and write the language natively or near-natively, and know how children and teenagers
actually type it in chat. Contribute or review in that language in public for a few weeks (a
pack entry, a translation, a review of an existing lesson), read the
[safeguarding policy](docs/SAFEGUARDING.md) and [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md), then ask
to be nominated in a proposal issue. If no one objects in 7 days, your name or handle goes in the
table above.

Under 18? You are very welcome as a contributor, and the youth advisory group is planned for you,
but maintainers are adults.

## Most wanted

1. A **Bangla** speaker to review `bn.json` and the Bangla red-team items, and help find real,
   non-abusive Bangla chat that Ward Lite can learn from.
2. An **Urdu** speaker to review the Urdu interface, lessons and stories.
3. **Roman Urdu** and **Hinglish** speakers to review those packs and their false alarms
   (friendly "pagal", "gadha", "kamina").
4. A second person for every language above, so no word is added on one person's say-so.

Start with the **Translation** or **Slang word** issue form, or see
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

# Seed issues (drafts)

> **Drafts, not yet opened on GitHub.** These are first issues for new contributors, written so a
> maintainer can copy each one into a new issue. Each is small, has a clear "done", and needs no
> access to real children's data. Suggested labels are given, but the labels may not exist yet.

Every issue opened from this file should keep the line: **Never paste a real child's chat, name,
photo, school or phone number in this issue or its pull request.**

---

## 1. Spaced-out "k y s" slips past the word lists

**Labels:** `good first issue`, `slang-pack`, `engine`

The joining rule in `normalize()` only joins single letters separated by spaces when there are
four or more, so "k y s" (telling someone to kill themselves) is never matched, and neither the
word lists nor Ward Lite flag it ([docs/REDTEAM.md](REDTEAM.md), item `en-004`). Three-letter
joining would also join harmless runs like "i m ok", so the fix needs care.

**Done when:** a spaced self-harm initialism of three letters is matched, an engine test shows
it, and a test shows ordinary three-letter runs ("i m ok", "u r ok") are not flagged. Don't add
the red-team message itself to any test or pack; write your own examples.

**Files:** `packages/engine/src/normalize.ts`, `packages/engine/src/engine.test.ts`.

## 2. Wilson intervals on the scorecard and red-team tables

**Labels:** `good first issue`, `eval`

The red-team set has 14 to 36 messages per language and side, and some cells have 2. A
percentage with no interval reads as more certain than it is.

**Done when:** the tables written by `eval/redteam/run.ts` (and, if simple, `eval/run.ts`) show a
95% Wilson interval next to each rate, and the method section says what the interval means.
No numbers change otherwise.

**Files:** `eval/redteam/run.ts`, `eval/run.ts`.

## 3. Review the Bangla slang pack (native speaker wanted)

**Labels:** `help wanted`, `slang-pack`, `language:bn`

`packages/engine/packs/bn.json` has 30 entries in Bangla script and romanised Bangla, written by
someone who does not speak Bangla natively. It has never been reviewed.

**Done when:** a Bangla speaker has gone through every entry and said, in the issue or a pull
request, whether its meaning, category and severity are right, which ones are also everyday words
(and so cause false alarms), and which common words are missing. Changes go in through the
[slang-pack review](../CONTRIBUTING.md#how-slang-pack-changes-are-reviewed).

## 4. Review the Urdu lessons and stories (native speaker wanted)

**Labels:** `help wanted`, `translation`, `language:ur`

The Urdu lessons and stories (`packages/lessons/src/units.ur.ts`, `stories.ur.ts`) and the Urdu
interface (`apps/web/src/i18n/ur.ts`) were written without a native speaker's review.

**Done when:** a reviewer has read one unit (say, *Spot it*) in all three age bands and listed
anything unnatural, too formal for a child, or that could carry an unintended meaning, with
suggested fixes. One unit per issue is fine; open another for the next.

## 5. Helpline numbers: a source and a date for every entry

**Labels:** `good first issue`, `helpline`

Helplines live in `apps/web/src/lib/help.ts`. The file says they were checked on 2026-10-29, but
individual entries don't say where each number came from.

**Done when:** each `HelpLine` has a `source` (a URL) and a `verifiedAt` date, a test fails if
either is missing, and the existing numbers are filled in from the sources they were checked
against. No number changes in this issue unless a source shows it is wrong (then say so in the
pull request).

**Files:** `apps/web/src/lib/help.ts`, `apps/web/src/lib/help.test.ts`.

## 6. Emoji stand-ins for appearance insults

**Labels:** `slang-pack`, `engine`, `proposal`

Animal emoji used as insults (🐷, 🐘, 🐒, 🐄) get past every phone layer
([docs/REDTEAM.md](REDTEAM.md), item 8). They are also used kindly all the time, so a plain
word-list entry would cause many false alarms.

**Done when:** there is a short written proposal in the issue for how Ward could treat an emoji
aimed at a person (for example, only next to "dekho", "look at" or a name), with made-up examples
on both sides, and a maintainer has agreed or declined. Code can follow in another issue.

## 7. Hinglish pack: add common words, with false-alarm notes

**Labels:** `help wanted`, `slang-pack`, `language:hi-Latn`

`packages/engine/packs/hi-Latn.json` has only 19 entries. The red-team set shows common
initialisms and insults it misses.

**Done when:** a Hinglish speaker proposes up to 15 words children actually use, each with a
meaning, category, severity and a note on whether it is used kindly between friends, and a second
speaker has reviewed them. Don't take words from the red-team set or the scorecard's test data.

## 8. Run the Urdu read-aloud on a real Android phone

**Labels:** `help wanted`, `accessibility`, `android`

Urdu read-aloud uses the device's own text-to-speech. It has not been tested inside the Android
app's WebView, where it may be silent.

**Done when:** someone has built the debug APK (see the README's [Run it](../README.md#run-it)),
switched Ward to Urdu, pressed Listen on a lesson, and reported in the issue the phone model,
Android version, and whether it spoke, with no screenshots of real chats.

## 9. Check Ward with a screen reader

**Labels:** `help wanted`, `accessibility`

Nobody has used Ward with TalkBack, VoiceOver or NVDA from start to finish.

**Done when:** someone has gone through onboarding, one check of a made-up chat, and one lesson
with a screen reader, and listed in the issue every place where focus got lost, a button had no
name, or feedback was silent. Fixes can be separate issues.

---

## Not seed issues

Some open work is not suitable for a first contribution, because it needs a decision from the
project's owner or a qualified person: the content licence, the safeguarding lead, ElevenLabs'
terms, replacing the SentNoB training data, and anything that changes what Ward does when it sees
danger. Those are tracked in [DPG.md](DPG.md#placeholders-in-this-file) and
[GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md).
